content.text: Cats ingest oocysts (soil · tissues of small prey) → replicate in feline intestine → excreted in feces → humans ingest (fecal-oral) → oocysts rupture → sporozoites → tachyzoites (blood & lymph → tissues) → bradyzoites in tissue cysts (chronic stage)
Congenital: tachyzoites cross placenta after maternal infect during preg
early GA: ↓transmission risk but ↑severity - later GA: ↑transmission but ↓severity
Transmission routes: aerosol · direct contact · fomites · oral · vector-borne - toxo: mother fecal-oral → baby transplacental (vertical)
•aerosol: resp droplets/particles (breathing · coughing · sneezing · talking · intubation · bronchoscopy · ventilation · suctioning) - influenza · COVID-19 · measles · varicella · TB · smallpox
•direct contact: tissues/fluids via mucous membranes · open wounds · bites · punctures · scratches - S. aureus · HIV · HSV · rabies
•fomite: inanimate object harboring pathogens - doorknobs · exam tables · medical equipment · clothing
ddx Schistosoma haematobium: parasite MC assoc w bladder CA
Other: jaundice · thrombocytopenia · anemia · fever · HSM · LAD
Untreated → ↑risk long-term sequelae even if mild/subclinical:
•chorioretinitis = MC long-term sequela - painless blurred vision - comp: vision loss · retinal detachment · cataracts · glaucoma
•motor & cerebellar dysfun · intellectual disability · sz · SNHL
•CSF PCR for T. gondii = gold standard
Test if: past or active maternal toxo · newborn clinical findings · ⊕ newborn screening Toxoplasma Ab
Suspected: regular eye exams · neuro eval · LP · neuroimaging
CT: focal brain lesions · IC calcifications · ventriculomegaly · cortical atrophy · hydrocephalus
•add prednisone if CSF protein >1g/dL or sight-threatening chorioretinitis
•early tx → much better prognosis - eradicates tachyzoites only (⍉bradyzoites) - untreated: poor (~93% intellectual disability)
•monitor closely for ocular or CNS dz
Prevention (maternal): ⍉raw or undercooked meat · wash fruits & vegetables · ⍉change cat litter
Highest risk of transmission in primary & 2ndry dz
of body fluids · placenta or cord
ALWAYS treated w PCN even if allergic
•fetus: transplacental - highest CRS risk <10wks GA (1st TM) · minimal risk after 18–20wks GA
•maternal infect → fetal death · preterm delivery · CRS
only teratogenic exanthem (vs mumps · roseola · rubeola)
: fever + rash (starts on face, then trunk & limbs)

can affect any organ: FGR · infantile glaucoma · pigmentary retinopathy · neonatal PNA · HSM · petechiae & purpura (blueberry muffin rash) · hemolytic anemia · thrombocytopenia · endocrine dz (DM · thyroid dz) · progressive panencephalitis
Suspect: mom w documented/suspected rubella in preg · infant w FGR · referred hearing screen · CRS manifestations → serologic rubella IgM
Also: CBC · LFTs · long-bone XR · ophtho eval · audiology eval · neuroimaging · LP · echo
•antivirals & biologics ⍉effect on course - supportive care & surveillance = mainstays
•close follow-up: hearing loss · developmental abnl · later ocular & endocrine dz
Prevention: rubella vax · test preg pts for rubella (maternal immunity) · educate nonimmune preg pts to avoid exposure
Common neonatal infect - leading cause of nonhereditary SNHL in newborns
Herpesvirus family · part of TORCH (toxo · other (syphilis) · rubella · CMV · HSV)
Maternal infect MC ← close contact w young children (aSx spread)
Vertical transmission risk ↑ w primary (vs recurrent/reactivated) maternal infect → infants more likely Sx @ birth
CMV = MCC of blindness in HIV pts
~10% Sx @ birth: petechiae · jaundice · hepatosplenomegaly · SGA · microcephaly · SNHL · lethargy · poor suck · chorioretinitis · sz · hemolytic anemia · PNA
Blueberry muffin rash: purpura/petechial rash - spotted blue or purple
SNHL in up to 1/2 of Sx infants - may be detectable @ birth, but ~1/3 have delayed onset
⍉macrocephaly (→ hydrocephalus · encephalopathy · metabolic dx) · hypotonia more often neuro dz (CP · musc dystrophy) · cyanosis ⍉CMV (→ CHD: TOF · TGA)
•U/S also: ventriculomegaly · microcephaly · hyperechogenic fetal bowel · FGR · ascites · hepatosplenomegaly · pleural effusion
viral cx of urine or saliva
•tx if virologically confirmed + ≥1 end-organ system involved (Sx infants only) → limit hearing/neurodevelopmental decline - most successful if started w.in 1st 30d of life
•⍉consensus for isolated hearing loss w.o other Sx
Prevention: ⍉vax - hygiene counseling (handwashing · ⍉sharing utensils/saliva w young children) - universal screening ⍉recommended (ACOG)

Maternal: immunocompetent → supportive care + MFM referral (⍉FDA-approved tx - high-dose valacyclovir promising but ⍉approved/⍉ACOG-recommended) - IS (AIDS/transplant): ganciclovir · valganciclovir · foscarnet for CMV dz, ⍉fetal prevention
Fetal: ⍉FDA-approved tx - in utero valacyclovir investigational
Majority of neonatal HSV infect are acquired perinatally - via an infected maternal genital tract
Neonatal HSV rare - USU several days after birth
Nonspecific systemic sxs: fever · ↓activity · poor feeding - grouped vesicles on an erythematous base
Multinucleated giant cells on Wright-stained Tzanck smear of vesicle contents = primary HSV skin infect
